name: Fetch
description: Fetch web pages with a real JS-rendering headless browser. Tool: Fetch.

tool.name: Fetch
tool.description: Fetch a webpage and return its rendered content. Use it when you know the URL, or when the page needs JavaScript to render and you want clean markdown. Do not use it to search without a URL, to read a local file, or when the user already pasted the content. Every call renders with anti-detection hardening on and that is not a parameter. Returns the page text in `content`.

url.description: The page URL. Must start with http:// or https://. Max 4096 chars.

format.description: Output format. `markdown` is the default for reading articles and docs. `text` for prose. `html` for markup. `links` to crawl a page. `accessibility` for a structure tree. `original` for raw bytes.

selector.description: Optional CSS selector. The browser waits for this element before returning. Useful for SPAs where the interesting content arrives after initial load.

eval.description: Optional JavaScript expression to evaluate in the page context. By default its value is returned instead of the page body. Use eval_mode='page' to evaluate first and then return the resulting page dump.

eval_mode.description: Optional return mode for eval. When omitted, eval alone returns its value while selector plus eval implies 'page'. 'value' returns the expression result. 'page' evaluates, settles page work, then returns the requested format.

wait_until.description: When to consider navigation complete. `domcontentloaded` is the default and the safe choice. `load` waits for every subresource and races anti-bot scripts. `networkidle0` waits for 500ms of quiet and suits a SPA.

timeout_sec.description: Navigation timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow or dynamic pages.

cleanup.description: Whitespace cleanup for markdown and text only. `basic` is the default and keeps single blank lines. `aggressive` folds whitespace and drops blanks, so use it on a noisy page. `off` is verbatim.

session.description: Session name to keep cookies and localStorage. It must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}$. The directory is sandboxed, so a path fails. An empty string opts out. Cookies and tokens are stored as plain JSON on disk, so do not put the user identity in the name. Make one Fetch call at a time per session.
